record.paper_title: On open problems based on fuzzy filters of pseudo BCK-algebras
record.context_brief: Characterizing implicative pseudo-BCK algebras by pseudo-filters
record.original_question: Let A be a pseudo-BCK algebra with binary operations ⇀ and ⇝ and top element 1. Call A an implicative pseudo-BCK algebra when, for every x and y in A, the identities (x ⇝ y) ⇀ x = x and (x ⇀ y) ⇝ x = x hold. A nonempty subset F of A is a pseudo-filter when it is upward closed and satisfies the closure rule that x in F together with either x ⇀ y in F or x ⇝ y in F implies y in F. A pseudo-filter F is Boolean when (x ⇀ y) ⇝ x in F implies x in F and (x ⇝ y) ⇀ x in F implies x in F for all x,y; it is implicative when (x ⇀ y) ⇀ x in F implies x in F and (x ⇝ y) ⇝ x in F implies x in F for all x,y. Prove or disprove the proposed characterization that A is an implicative pseudo-BCK algebra if and only if every pseudo-filter of A is a Boolean filter, equivalently if and only if every pseudo-filter of A is an implicative pseudo-filter.

evidence.quote: Prove or negate the following conclusion
A pseudo-BCK algebra is an implicative pseudo-BCK algebra

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(A,\rightharpoonup,\rightsquigarrow,1)$ be a pseudo-BCK algebra, where $\rightharpoonup$ and $\rightsquigarrow$ are binary operations and $1$ is the top element with respect to the induced order $x\le y\iff x\rightharpoonup y=1\iff x\rightsquigarrow y=1$. Call $A$ an implicative pseudo-BCK algebra if, for all $x,y\in A$,
$$(x\rightsquigarrow y)\rightharpoonup x=x\quad\text{and}\quad(x\rightharpoonup y)\rightsquigarrow x=x.$$
A nonempty subset $F\subseteq A$ is a pseudo-filter if it is upward closed (with respect to $\le$) and, for all $x,y\in A$, $x\in F$ together with $x\rightharpoonup y\in F$ or $x\rightsquigarrow y\in F$ implies $y\in F$. A pseudo-filter $F$ is called:
- a Boolean filter if for all $x,y\in A$, $(x\rightharpoonup y)\rightsquigarrow x\in F\Rightarrow x\in F$ and $(x\rightsquigarrow y)\rightharpoonup x\in F\Rightarrow x\in F$;
- an implicative pseudo-filter if for all $x,y\in A$, $(x\rightharpoonup y)\rightharpoonup x\in F\Rightarrow x\in F$ and $(x\rightsquigarrow y)\rightsquigarrow x\in F\Rightarrow x\in F$.

Prove or disprove: $A$ is an implicative pseudo-BCK algebra if and only if every pseudo-filter of $A$ is a Boolean filter, and equivalently if and only if every pseudo-filter of $A$ is an implicative pseudo-filter.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work on filter theory in pseudo-BCK algebras reports complete solutions to this open problem, establishing that a pseudo-BCK algebra is implicative if and only if every pseudo-filter is a Boolean (equivalently, implicative) filter, with the equivalence of Boolean and implicative pseudo-filters proved in the (bounded) pseudo-BCK setting.
